name: Imago's Clinic
descriptionTemplate: {Team Unique}: At the start of exploration, add 1 {derived:Imago's Clinic} to the deck. {derived:Insect Taxidermy}
lore:
Rain and night had wrapped themselves around the city of Londinium. A perfectly ordinary detective from the very bottom rung of the ladder knocked on the door of this room. He had been sent to investigate a suspect, yet in the blink of an eye, he found himself already sitting at the table.

The dim yellow lamp cast the shadow of an insect onto the wall, its feelers trembling.

"You know, Doctor, I didn't even want this assignment... but I came anyway. For myself, not for anyone else, damn them all... Yes, that must be it!"

Glittering dust drifted down through the lamplight like crumbs of a soul, or crumbs of a biscuit that had been dunked in far too much sugar.

"My boss told me this job would be easy—that pig! He always says that. Last time he said it, my partner died. The time before that, I got two ribs broken!"

The butterfly fluttered up and down, dancing, because it longed to confess, longed to let go, longed to be free.

"Ha! I've interrogated so many suspects who swore they had their reasons. They complained to me, shouted at me, begged me to understand, but who understands my suffering? Doctor, I know you can work wonders. Please, just listen to me a little longer..."

<Italic:Snap.> Just as the butterfly reached the top of its flight, an invisible blade pierced its wings and made it eternal, frozen at its most beautiful moment. Titled <Italic:A Certain Man's Suffering>, it was a rare piece of art no collector would miss.

Clementine simply smiled and listened. The patient, who was still talking and showed no sign of stopping, had no idea that every thought buried deep in his heart, along with a few he had never actually had, was being squeezed out of him down to the very last drop.

Nor did he know that his twisted face and his dreadful howl were, at that very moment, being frozen in place, for the person across the table to admire and savor again and again.

...

"What a delightful session. If any of your colleagues have similar troubles, do send them my way."

That day, Clementine's psychology practice gained a new and rather special butterfly specimen. It would not be the last. The lovingly crafted display cabinet still had plenty of room, enough for more, and more, and more...

The hunter sat at the table, eyes half-closed and contented. She meant to savor this particular pain for a good long while. She never had to lure anyone. People always delivered their honey-sweet feelings to her in person, and quite often forgot why they had come in the first place.

The rain kept falling, covering up a great many sounds that shouldn't have been there. But the crisp crack of an insect breaking out of its cocoon, and the hum that called out to chaos, always arrived right on time, weaving together high above the city into a symphony that belonged to her and her kind alone. Every specimen was a song about suffering.
